Fix the accounts-broker sign-in and verify-email pages rendering their shared CSS as visible page text: the style block was concatenated into the head without a `<style>` element, so browsers hoisted the raw CSS into the body and the pages rendered unstyled.

Authorize shared-workspace relay tunnels per explicit label: the frps NewProxy check now requires every claimed customDomain to be a single DNS label directly under the share's domain (rejecting the bare domain and the wildcard), matching the workspace's switch to explicit per-service claims. The accounts broker's share-authorize handoff now delivers its login callback to a validated ``callback_origin`` (the workspace's dedicated auth label, required to be exactly one label under the share's domain, mirroring the NewProxy model) instead of the bare domain, and preserves the full ``next`` deep-link when it stays on the workspace -- both host-bearing values are checked against the share's domain so a signed token can never be redirected off-domain.

Add "Continue with Google" to the accounts broker's share login page. Accounts created via Google OAuth have no password and previously could not open a share at all; the broker now offers the provider's own browser flow (`/share/oauth/google/start` -> Google -> `/share/oauth/google/callback`), which creates the SuperTokens session and resumes the pending share authorization exactly like the password form. The flow's state is a self-contained signed token (nonce + resume path) bound to a browser cookie against login CSRF, so it works across the connector's concurrent Modal containers with no server-side pending-flow state. Configured via a new Web-application Google OAuth client in the sharing secret (`BROKER_GOOGLE_CLIENT_ID`/`BROKER_GOOGLE_CLIENT_SECRET`); the button is hidden when unconfigured, and an email already registered with a password is refused with a pointer back to the password form (one-account-per-email, shared with the CLI flow).
